title: Hail, full of grace: fountain, flower, meadow, vine, field

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 12, col. D, to p. 13, col. A (PDF pp. 36-37)

source_text: Ave gratia plena, fons lucis, qui cunctos in ipsum credentes illuminat. Ave gratia plena, intelligibilis solis oriens, et flos vitae immaculatus. Ave gratia plena, pratum fragrantissimum. Ave gratia plena, vitis semper vigens; quae animas glorificantium te laetificas. Ave gratia plena, ager qui non exaratus fructus profert pulcherrimos: Secundum naturam quidem, eo quod more nostro, et tempore motus, gestationisque servato protulisti: at praeter naturam, aut potius supra naturam; quia superne divinum Verbum advenit, et in sancto tuo utero Adamum reformavit. Ac fecunditatem quidem, Spiritus Sanctus sanctae virgini praebuit: verum autem corpus ex eius corpore assumptum est.
pass_a_gloss: Hail full of grace, fountain of light (fons lucis), which enlightens (illuminat) all believing in Him. Hail full of grace, rising (oriens) of the intelligible/spiritual sun (intelligibilis sol), and immaculate flower of life (flos vitae immaculatus). Hail full of grace, most fragrant meadow (pratum fragrantissimum). Hail full of grace, ever-flourishing vine (vitis semper vigens); which gladdens (laetificas) the souls of those glorifying you. Hail full of grace, field (ager) which not ploughed (non exaratus) brings forth (profert) most beautiful fruits: according to nature (secundum naturam) indeed, in that in our manner (more nostro), and the time of movement (tempus motus) and of carrying (gestatio) being kept (servato), you brought forth (protulisti): but beyond nature (praeter naturam), or rather above nature (supra naturam); because from above (superne) the divine Word came (advenit), and in your holy womb (uterus) re-formed (reformavit) Adam. And fruitfulness (fecunditas) indeed the Holy Spirit supplied (praebuit) to the holy virgin: but the true body (verum corpus) from her body was taken (assumptum est).

choices.choice: 'tempore motus, gestationisque servato' (as printed) rendered 'keeping the time of the child's stirring and of carrying';
'intelligibilis solis oriens' rendered 'dawning of the spiritual Sun' (intelligibilis = known by the mind, not the visible sun); the partly legible margin variant ('solis iustitiae'?) not adopted.

pass_b_english: Hail, full of grace, fountain of light that enlightens all who believe in Him. Hail, full of grace, dawning of the spiritual Sun, and spotless flower of life. Hail, full of grace, most fragrant meadow. Hail, full of grace, ever-flourishing vine, who gladden the souls of those who glorify you. Hail, full of grace, field that bears the fairest fruits without being ploughed.

Your bearing was according to nature, in that you brought forth in our manner, keeping the time of the child's stirring and of carrying; but beyond nature, or rather above nature, because the divine Word came from on high and in your holy womb formed Adam anew. The Holy Spirit gave the holy Virgin her fruitfulness; but the true body was taken from her body.
notes: Second paragraph opens 'Your bearing was according to nature' to carry the elliptical 'Secundum naturam quidem ... protulisti' as a full sentence; it supplies no new idea beyond protulisti. 'tempore motus, gestationisque servato' (as printed) rendered 'keeping the time of the child's stirring and of carrying'; 'the child's' makes explicit what motus means here (doubtful reading, see source note). 'quidem ... autem' pairs fecunditatem with corpus, so 'verum' is taken as the adjective ('the true body'), not as the conjunction 'but'. 'intelligibilis solis oriens' rendered 'dawning of the spiritual Sun' (intelligibilis = known by the mind, not the visible sun); the partly legible margin variant ('solis iustitiae'?) not adopted. 'fons lucis, qui ... illuminat' keeps the print's third person; 'in ipsum' = Christ. No Scripture cited: the titles are the author's own images.
source_notes: PDF p. 36 = printed p. 12, col. D, to PDF p. 37 = printed p. 13, col. A. Margin at 'solis oriens': a variant beginning 'al. soli[s] iu[stitiae] ...', small and only partly legible. 'tempore motus' as printed (sense: the due time of movement and carrying kept). 'fecunditatem' printed 'foecunditatem'. After 'reformavit' the print has a stop and a caret-like mark before 'ac'.
